title: Tensor product of a geometrically normal algebra and a normal algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $A$ and $B$ be commutative $k$-algebras. Assume $A$ is geometrically normal over $k$, meaning that for every field extension $E/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] the commutative tensor-product algebra $A\otimes_k E$ is a normal ring. Assume $B$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Then $A\otimes_k B$ is a normal ring: each of its prime localizations is an integrally closed domain. Tensor products are commutative tensor-product algebras [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with $(a\otimes b)(a^{\prime}\otimes b^{\prime})=aa^{\prime}\otimes bb^{\prime}$ and unit $1\otimes1$. No Noetherian, finite-type, domain or nonzero hypothesis is imposed on $A$ or $B$.

proof.text: Geometric normality implies normality of A by testing on a universe lift of the base field k and transporting along the right-unit tensor equivalence. Normality and geometric normality are preserved by localization: prime localizations of a localization identify with prime localizations of the original ring, and localization commutes with tensor-product scalar extension.

Fix a prime r of A tensor_k B and contract it to p in A and q in B. The rings A_p and B_q are normal domains; A_p remains geometrically normal. Apply the normal-domain case to conclude A_p tensor_k B_q is normal.

Localizing the two tensor factors in succession inverts elements outside r, by contraction. Extend r through each localization and identify its final prime localization with the original tensor-product localization at r. Descend the normality just proved through these localization identifications. This works prime by prime; for a zero algebra there is no prime and the conclusion is vacuous.
